item.title: After Draymond Green's ejection, galvanized Warriors hang on to beat Suns for fifth straight win
item.description: Phoenix Suns guard Jalen Green attempts to pass the ball while being guarded by the Warriors' Brandin Podziemski during the first half Monday. (Jed Jacobsohn/AP Photo/Jed Jacobsohn) This, as crew chief Sean Wright told the crowd at Chase Center, was a "throwdown." There was simply no more generous way to put it, even by the buttoned-up linguistic standards of an NBA official. Draymond Green had struck again. Actually, it was more of a push. Young Suns big man Khaman Maluach bumped Green off his spot early in the third quarter of an eventual 116-113 Golden State win, with enough force to send him sprawling. A pass to Maluach came, and one could see Green's gears turning the moment he stood, beelining back in front of Maluach and wrapping him up. Then came the throwdown, Green flinging the 7-foot-1, 250-pound Maluach to the hardwood and standing over him after. Phoenix forward Dillon Brooks - feign surprise here - bolted up to go nose-to-nose with Green, a savvy and incredibly consequential move from a longtime Warriors heel. Green was dinged for a technical on the Maluach scuffle and another technical on the face-off with Brooks, and sat on the bench, pensive, as Wright announced he'd been ejected. Suddenly, the loss of their emotional heartbeat brought emotion. Green and running mate Stephen Curry had come out utterly flat after resting Sunday night on the front-end of a back-to-back, as Green finished with just four points and two assists in a disengaged 17 minutes. But Chase suddenly roared to life with Golden State down 10 - and after second-half flurries by Curry and Brandin Podziemski to pull the Warriors back came a defensive stand that would've made Green proud. Up four under two minutes, Curry and De'Anthony Melton got back-to-back steals. Melton, then, drew a charge on Suns star Devin Booker to knock him out with six fouls. And rookie Yaxel Lendeborg sent away a running layup by Suns guard Jalen Green, as the Warriors hung on after a free-throw battle to improve to 5-3. item.title: The baffling question surrounding Unai Emery and Aston Villa ahead of Barcelona showdown
item.description: It is the biggest club from England’s second city against the biggest from Spain’s. And if the similarities between Birmingham and Barcelona may end there – the Brummie separatist movement is rather less prominent that its Catalan counterpart, for instance – then a trip to Camp Nou is both a sign of a new eminence and part of a broader question about Aston Villa ’s status. In footballing terms, England’s second city has often tended to be Manchester, Liverpool or London. The notion that Villa will forever lie further down the footballing food chain seemed to underpin Jamie Carragher’s somewhat derogatory comments last week; even if Villa’s threat to sue the pundit , signed by chairman Nassef Sawiris, struck many as frankly silly. Meanwhile, Unai Emery wore his Villa blazer to the Ballon d’Or ceremony last week. It could be interpreted as a gesture of his enduring loyalty, amid the possibility the Manchester United job will become vacant ; but perhaps he simply liked the garment. Unai Emery was repping Aston Villa at last week’s Ballon d’Or (AFP/Getty) Whichever, Villa may have one of the two finest managers currently working in the Premier League, along with Emery’s fellow Basque Mikel Arteta, and one of the best in Europe; his record five Europa League wins indicates as much. Villa’s renaissance has been inspired by Emery and can feel reliant upon him. They could be a club who are establishing themselves as a regular presence on such nights or one who may not been seen again at Camp Nou for decades; in March, Newcastle, like Villa now, in a second Champions League campaign in three seasons, lost 7-2 to Barcelona. It remains to be seen if they will return any time soon. For Villa, this is a first game against Barcelona at their iconic stadium for 43 years, since a Super Cup defeat; Villa were European champions then and won the second leg 3-0. It was their last continental trophy until Emery’s side beat Freiburg in May . Villa are ticking off the clashes with the European superpowers. Two years ago, they renewed acquaintances with Bayern Munich and, as they did in the 1982 European Cup final, beat them 1-0 . They ran Paris Saint-Germain close in the 2025 quarter-finals , only narrowly lost to them in this summer’s Super Cup and face them again next month. It only really leaves Real Madrid of the current elite to face. item.title: The ‘magical night’ Man United must replicate to halt slide into chaos
item.description: When the Champions League draw pitted Manchester United against Roma , the more nostalgic were transported back 20 seasons. To a night that, ultimately, proved a staging post on Sir Alex Ferguson’s way to conquering Europe the following season. To a European Cup win that, in its margin, has only been bettered in United’s history by the Busby Babes’ 10-0 demolition of Anderlecht in 1956. To the only time in 464 appearances for United that Michael Carrick scored twice. In 2007, United faced a Roma side that included the World Cup winners Francesco Totti and Daniele de Rossi. They thrashed them 7-1. “A magical night,” Carrick recalled. “It was one of the best nights, one of the best games, one of the best atmospheres I've been fortunate enough to witness. So the fact that I scored a couple and that was very unusual gives me great, great memories, but it was more the actual whole the emotion of the night. It was a special one.” Kobbie Mainoo’s return offers a boost to Michael Carrick and his struggling side (PA) But Carrick’s initial response had been: “Long time ago, hey?” Increasingly, that comment could be applied to many of the good times: to the heady days in spring when he won 12 of his first 17 games after returning to Old Trafford. Now, nine without a win, beaten in each of the last three, Carrick could do with recapturing some of the magic he and his teammates produced to inflict Roma’s record European defeat. Although, as Gian Piero Gasperini’s team are third in Serie A and, two weeks ago, United lost 4-1 to the side now fourth in the Italian top flight, it feels unlikely. But, almost two decades ago, United had lost consecutive games before welcoming Roma to Old Trafford. Things can change, quickly and dramatically. “You might think I'm crazy with the results we've had and what's going on, but I genuinely, really can't wait for the game,” said Carrick. And indeed, it may sound delusional; or, at the least, the words of a man who remembers what United was and imagines it could be again. But not, perhaps, with him as manager, or this group of players, or this hierarchy or these owners. item.title: Dodge Returns to NASCAR Cup Series in 2027 with Daytona 500 Debut
item.description: Dodge Returns to NASCAR in 2027 at Daytona 500 Stellantis Dodge is returning to NASCAR Cup Series competition and doing it big, with an all-new racecar set to debut at the Daytona 500 inFebruary of 2027, ending a 15-year absence from the top stock-car series. Tim Kuniskis, Stellantis head of American brands, announced the plan right after the preview of the Jeep Wrangler Scramber concept , on the eve of the 2026 Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) show in Las Vegas. “We’re going do it the way racers do it. We’re doing to all that research and development and testing and tuning. But we’re going to do it on track. We’re going back. Dodge is going back to NASCAR, and it’s not Daytona 2030, it’s Daytona 2027, in 3 months. Dodge is back in Cup, right now,” said Kunikisis. Stellantis head of American Brands Tim Kuniskis MotorTrend - MotorTrend Dodge’s last Cup season was 2012, when Brad Keselowski won the driver championship in a Dodge Charger for Penske Racing. The brand recorded its first Cup victory in 1953. Dodge has not identified the model or technical configuration it will use for its 2027 entry. Brad Keslelowski won the NASCAR Spring Cup Series championship in 2012, driving the No. 2 Miller Lite Dodge Charger for Penske Racing. MotorTrend - MotorTrend Kaulig Racing will serve as Dodge’s anchor team for. The team, which also fields Ram entries in the NASCAR Craftsman truck series, will announce its driver lineup for 2027 during NASCAR Championship Weekend at Homestead-Miami Speedway. Dodge SRT Racing will oversee the brand’s North American motorsports programs, including its NASCAR effort. Before the 2027 Cup season officially opens, the new racecar will make its debut at the Dodge Sno-Brawl at Five Flags Speedway in Pensacola, Florida on December 4, the day before the 59th annual Snowball Derby. First held in 1968, the Snowball Derby is a 300-lap Super Late Model race and one of short-track racing’s longest-running events. It regularly draws top short-track competitors and NASCAR drivers. At the Sno-Brawl, Dodge will reveal the car that will carry its livery in NASCAR Cup competition. Celebrity drivers will also compete head-to-head in identically prepared Dodge Charger late-model stock cars, in a separate event from the Snowball Derby’s main race. While Kuniskis announced the Daytona 500 racing debut, he did not disclose how many Cup cars Kaulig Racing will field or whether other teams will participate. Qualifying for the 69th Daytona 500 is on February 17, 2027 and the 200-lap, 500-mile race starts at 2:30pm ET on February 21, 2027, at the Daytona International Speedway, in Daytona Beach, Florida.

item.title: Thomaston girls soccer wins a Berkshire League championship thriller after 3 shootout saves
item.description: Members of the Thomaston girls soccer team celebrate after defeating Housatonic for the Berkshire League tournament championship on Monday, Nov. 2, 2026. (Steve Barlow/For Hearst Connecticut Media) WOODBURY – If the Thomaston girls soccer team printed its own money, the currency would say: "In Brynn we trust." Golden Bears junior keeper Brynn Beaudoin, the backbone of the team all season, came through again in a 2-1 victory over Housatonic in a Berkshire League tournament final that was decided in a penalty-kick shootout Monday night at Nonnewaug. In the rubber match between the two teams, Beaudoin not only stopped three Housy attempts in the shootout, but earlier made the play of the evening by smothering a penalty kick by the Mountaineers' Georgie Clayton with 6½ minutes left in regulation. "It's really just guessing," said Beaudoin, who had 13 saves for the night. "They're all amazing players. They can shoot very well, so you just guess and hope you're guessing right." Thomaston coach Greg Blasko will tell you it's more than just a guessing game. Intuition and instinct play roles, too. When the game went to the shootout round, he liked his team's chances. In fact, that was the strategy once the game went to two 5-minute overtimes. "As we were headed to overtime, that was the plan. Let's defend. Let's get to PK's. You've been practicing them. We've got a BL first-team All-Star goalkeeper. Why wouldn't we want to go to penalty kicks," Blasko said. "The plan came together." Through four kicks by each side, the shootout was tied, 2-2. Hannah Zuklie and and Kaylee Boulanger converted for Thomaston, while Leila Wiles and Emma Wiles were stymied. For Housatonic, Lainey Diorio and Attie Bergin converted, while Lyla Diorio and Kenzie Lotz were stopped by Beaudoin. On Thomaston's final attempt, freshman Kyla Lahey planted the ball in the upper left corner for her 31st goal of the season. On Housy's final attempt, Clayton's shot, with a slight assist by Beaudoin, hit the crossbar. "I was thinking if I make this, our team would win," said Lahey of her final shot. "I knew Brynn would save it and she did. I always trust Brynn." Lahey scored the first goal of the game with 10 minutes left in the first half by intercepting the ball and rocketing a shot through the fingers of Housy keeper Vi Salazar (nine saves). Three minutes later, the game was tied again after an own goal when Clayton's cross ricocheted in off Thomaston defender Emma Harkness. With 6:40 on the clock in regulation, Clayton was tripped in the penalty box and awarded a penalty kick. item.title: Panathinaikos sporting director predicts fiery atmosphere against Real Madrid in Athens: ‘It’s going to be impressive’
item.description: Panathinaikos sporting director predicts fiery atmosphere against Real Madrid in Athens: ‘It’s going to be impressive’ Real Madrid are currently in a great run of form – the best they have been in all season – and have the momentum firmly on their side. The win over Barcelona, who were hyped as the overwhelming favourites in El Clasico , appears to have taken the team’s confidence to a whole new level and the impact was visible in their recent outing. Taking to the field against Racing Santander at the weekend, Los Blancos not only dominated the game but delivered three crushing blows before half-time, thereby virtually sealing the result before the halfway stage. Now, they are set to return to action in the UEFA Champions League, where they travel to Greece to take on AEK Athens away from home. Greek side’s administrator speaks on the clash Greek side Panathinaikos’ sporting advisor Miguel Angel Corona, who also happens to be a former Real Madrid youth player, spoke to the media via Diario AS in a recent interview where he previewed the game between Real Madrid and AEK Athens. Miguel Angel Corona is predicting a tough night for Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) He praised Real Madrid for the momentum they have generated in recent weeks “They are a team with tremendous intensity, both in terms of match tempo and physical fitness,” he began. He then spoke highly of Real Madrid’s defence and attack, which have both performed at a great level in recent times. “Their centre-backs are very strong, and their two strikers, if they play together, are difficult to defend against because of their physical presence.” “However, Real Madrid’s attacking pace could make the difference,” he added. Real Madrid are in great form under Mourinho. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Real Madrid’s arrival in Greece to play a Champions League clash is a special occasion in Athens, and the former youth player spoke on how it would be an ‘impressive’ event. “It’s going to be impressive. In these nights, Greek football can show the rest of Europe that it has teams, fans and passion. They turn over. item.title: Hansi Flick confirms versatile Barcelona star’s return delayed until 2027
item.description: Hansi Flick confirms versatile Barcelona star’s return delayed until 2027 Barcelona will have to wait longer than initially expected to welcome Xavi Espart back from injury, with Hansi Flick indicating that the 19-year-old could remain unavailable until the first match of 2027. The defender is recovering from a syndesmosis injury to his right ankle sustained during the El Clasico defeat against Real Madrid on October 25, leaving the Catalan club without a versatile defensive option during an already difficult period for the squad. Flick provided an indication of Espart’s recovery timeline during his pre-match press conference ahead of Barcelona’s Champions League meeting with Aston Villa. Espart’s ankle injury proves more complicated for Barcelona Espart suffered the injury during Barcelona’s 1-2 defeat to Real Madrid at the Spotify Camp Nou, following a challenge involving Aurelien Tchouameni. The youngster was unable to continue and had to be replaced, with Alejandro Balde coming on as his replacement. Medical examinations subsequently confirmed damage to the syndesmosis joint in his right ankle. Barcelona announced on October 26 that the defender would be sidelined for approximately seven weeks, initially suggesting a possible return before the end of the calendar year. However, Flick’s comments indicate that the club could be without the teenager for considerably longer than that initial estimate. Barcelona in trouble? Barcelona are currently managing several defensive absences, with Andreas Christensen, Eric Garcia and Jules Kounde also unavailable. However, Flick expects those three players to return after the upcoming international break, leaving Espart with the longest projected recovery period among the defenders mentioned. “We have four injured players: Xavi Espart, Eric, Christensen and Kounde. Xavi might return at the start of 2027. Others are likely to return after the int’l break. Espart was injured against Real Madrid. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “It’s not easy to manage, but Frenkie is there, coming back from injury and willing to help, just like Brian Farinas,” said the manager during the pre-match press conference ahead of Aston Villa clash. Barcelona lose an important option in Flick’s defensive plans Espart’s absence is particularly relevant because of his versatility. The teenager has demonstrated an ability to operate on both sides of defence, giving Flick additional flexibility. His emergence has also been encouraging from an attacking perspective, as Espart registered two goals and two assists in nine appearances across competitions before sustaining the injury during the 2026-27 campaign. Barcelona have already faced defensive selection problems recently, and a strong option until 2027 now limits Flick’s options.

item.title: What Tommy Lloyd and Ivan Kharchenkov said after Arizona’s loss to UCLA
item.description: LAS VEGAS, NV - NOVEMBER 02: Arizona Wildcats guard Derek Dixon (7) and Arizona Wildcats center Motiejus Krivas (13) react after the Hall of Fame Series Las Vegas, a men's college basketball game between the Arizona Wildcats and the UCLA Bruins on November 2, 2026 at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, NV. (Photo by Brian Rothmuller/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images LAS VEGAS—Monday night marked the 185 th game for Tommy Lloyd as a head coach, but counting his 20-plus years as an assistant at Gonzaga he’s been on the bench for several hundred more. But only twice before had Lloyd been on the losing end of the first game of the season as a coach, and not since 2003. The 84-75 loss to UCLA at T-Mobile Arena was the first defeat for Arizona in an opener since 2006, resulting in a feeling Wildcat fans haven’t had in a long time. But if you thought Lloyd was going to freak out about the loss, think again. “There’s no panic after one game,” Lloyd said in his postgame press conference. “These seasons are long, and I know everyone has high hopes and wants everything to go perfect. But when you’ve been doing this for enough years, you know you’re in a very imperfect business, so just get get comfortable being challenged. And so I’m honestly really looking forward to seeing how we respond.” Our full game recap can be found here . Below is what Lloyd and Ivan Kharchenkov , who scored a career-high 38 points, said after the loss: Lloyd on the offense struggling much of the night: “UCLA is a great defensive team, and they came in with a game plan, and obviously kind of took us out of our rhythm, and we just couldn’t find it for for a while. That happens to teams, especially early in the season. We’ve got a lot of new guys playing new roles, and you kind of get punched in the face a little bit, and maybe you kind of lose your way. I’m proud of the way our guys fought back, but the incredible thing for me is—like listen, I wanted to win, of course—but I’m ready to move forward and just get better. item.title: Rajat Paliwal's 21st first-class ton: A century without knowing he was nearing one
item.description: NEW DELHI: Ravikant has kept Palam's Air Force Complex Ground ticking for the past 35 years. The chief ground staff member, he also doubles up as the scoreboard operator. But when cricket resumed after the COVID pandemic, he received an unusual request from the Services captain Rajat Paliwal: he did not want his name displayed on the scoreboard while batting. Ravikant, a little hesitant at first, agreed. "Sab ka apna apna hota hai. Kaptaan sahab ka farman aaya aur humne maan liya (Everyone has their own superstition. He made the request and I accepted it)," Ravikant said. On Monday, the 34-year-old Paliwal smashed his 21st first-class century to rescue Services, who were reeling at 27 for three, and took them to 266 on the opening day of their Ranji Trophy Group C clash against Delhi. He remained unbeaten on 111 off 196 balls. With no name appearing against Batsman 2 (Paliwal) on the scoreboard, the veteran batter had no way of knowing how close he was to his century. He eventually realised he had reached the milestone through the reaction of Delhi's fielders, who began closing in around him. "I got to know that I was getting closer to a century when I saw more fielders around me. I realised I had scored a hundred only through the reaction of the Delhi players," he told reporters at the end of the opening day. "I started this practice sometime after Covid. Sometimes, I used to feel a little nervous and lose my focus. The scoreboard draws attention, so I have taken it out of the picture entirely to concentrate only on the game," he added. This was Paliwal's highest score of the season so far, and he described it as particularly special. When he walked out to bat, Services were staring at the possibility of being bowled out for less than 100. But Paliwal stood up for his team, as he has done for nearly a decade-and-a-half. "This hundred is very special, especially because the team had lost four wickets for 44 runs and we needed this knock. The plan was for Porzingis to start and potentially rebuild his trade value. However, none of that has materialized. All Dallas needed to do was milk the clock. Minshew’s pass had been incomplete, and the Cardinals were probably going to try a field goal on the next play. Minshew threw a touchdown pass on the next play to cut the score from 27-17 to 27-24, and the comeback was on. Gary’s play cost the Cowboys the game, and he probably should be benched for it. Instead, when Brian Schottenheimer was asked about it on Monday, he said merely that Gary got a stern talking-to. As Clarence Hill of DLLS Cowboys noted, “How Did the Cowboys and Brian Schottenheimer hold Rashan Gary accountable following the egregious hit on the quarterback that gave the Cardinals a first down following a third down incompletion? With the Lakers looking for defenders who also have the ability to score, CBS Sports’ Sam Quinn believes they could make a trade for Orlando Magic guard Jalen Suggs. “The Magic are taking a big step -- or they're breaking up their core. item.description: Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images The Philadelphia 76ers have started the season in magnificent style, winning seven of their first eight games. The latest of those victories came against the Chicago Bulls on Monday night, when the Sixers stepped it up in the second half again. Jaylen Brown arguably had his best game yet with the 76ers, but he didn’t seem fully satisfied with how his side performed against the Bulls. Jaylen Brown issues warning to Philadelphia 76ers teammates The 76ers have shown the impressive trait of stepping it up late in games after slow starts. In fact, in five of their seven wins so far this season, the Sixers weren’t great in the first half but showed their class by going up a level after the break to secure those victories. That is undoubtedly a great trait to have, but Brown has warned his teammates that this could come back to bite them in tougher games. The former Boston Celtics star made it clear that he doesn’t like these slow starts and urged his teammates to be at it from the first whistle. When a reporter asked Brown if the ability to flip the switch in second halves gives the Sixers confidence, he replied: “No. I don’t like that we have that. “It’s good that we have shown the potential, but we’ve got to keep that switch on. It doesn’t work like that, where you just flip the switch and catch up to it. It can bite us against a better team, or on a night that we’re not being as crisp on offence. “So, there can’t be a switch just because we’re playing a lesser opponent or just because whatever the case may be. We have got to make sure that mentality is from the beginning to the end. Can’t skip any steps.” Brown is spot on. The Sixers’ ability to turn games on their head in the second half is definitely impressive, but they can’t rely on that in every game. The focus has to be on dominating the first and second quarters just as well as they do in the fourth. If they do that, they will become even bigger favourites to make the NBA Finals this year. item.title: The referee who became a role model after bouncing back from Diaz error
item.description: If anyone can talk about the highs and lows of being a referee, it is Darren England. Three years ago, when acting as the video assistant referee (VAR), a blunder in a game between Tottenham and Liverpool stalled his career for months. Luis Diaz scored for Liverpool, but his goal was flagged as offside. In a lapse of concentration, and despite the VAR image showing Diaz was onside, England said "check complete". The goal remained disallowed. The South Yorkshire official suddenly found not only himself in the full glare of the media, but his family too. "Refereeing is about low points and high points," England tells BBC Sport. "It's a rollercoaster of emotions. "That was a low point. The lowest point, of course." Today, the 40-year-old's career is revived. He is considered one of the most-trusted referees in the Premier League - both on the field and as a VAR. Throughout 2026, England has regularly been given some of English football's biggest matches - including Manchester City's 1-0 win over Chelsea in the FA Cup final. "So we flip it," England says, moving the conversation along to the game at Wembley. "That was a huge high for me, the pinnacle as a referee." And on Tuesday, England has been promoted to a VAR in the Champions League for the first time, as Galatasaray take on Stuttgart. This is the story of his rejuvenation. In a 'really difficult place' after Diaz error Darren England made it to the Premier League as an assistant referee before becoming a referee, working his way back up from the National League [Getty Images] The game has changed immeasurably in the 11 years since England swapped his flag for a whistle. England says referees are now "dressed like RoboCop" as they carry so much additional equipment, such as communication devices. The biggest change has been the introduction of VAR, which had only been in the Premier League for a few months when England refereed Southampton v Wolves in January 2020. "It's certainly not changed the way I make decisions," England insists. "If I play on on a penalty decision, some people think the perception is 'oh you're waiting for VAR to get involved'. "No, I've played on because I don't think it's a penalty. "But I would rather be driving home from a game now thinking, 'OK, I misread it live, I've had the opportunity to go to the screen and we've corrected it'." England underlines this, rejecting the notion that referees "don't care about football" when they get a decision wrong. "It couldn't be further away from the truth," he says. "It's a myth that we go home, we switch off. "It spoils your weekend if you make a decision that's had a big impact in the game. "It can spoil it for longer, of course." England knows this better than most. From the VAR audio of the Diaz incident, it was clear England and his assistant VAR, Dan Cook were immediately aware they had made a huge mistake. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . LeBron James is approaching the age of 42 and is enjoying every single second he has left on an NBA court. On Monday night, in the third quarter of the Philadelphia 76ers ’ 126-107 victory over the Chicago Bulls, he continued his quirky era by taking a sip of wine from a fan’s cup in the middle of the game after he ran all the way to the baseline on a botched possession. This was a lighthearted moment that drew some laughter at Xfinity Mobile Arena, as it is becoming very evident that James is playing loose and carefree and does not care that much at all anymore about what other people think. However, this wine-sipping “incident”, so to speak, has become a reason for some, including Barstool Sports owner Dave Portnoy, to dish out some criticism the 76ers star’s way. Portnoy, in a rant on his X account, accused James of setting a poor example for children after he consumed alcohol in the middle of an NBA game. Who cares the example it sets for kids that you need to be drunk to play sports?” Portnoy wrote. If anybody else did this they’d be checked into AA but because it’s Bron Bron Sportcenter will do an hour special on it. Who cares the example it sets for kids that you need to be drunk to play sports? pic.twitter.com/gKhF7SqyIa — Dave Portnoy (@stoolpresidente) November 3, 2026 Drinking while on the job is a frowned-upon practice in workplaces, so it’s a bit understandable as to where Portnoy is coming from.
